item.title: Elevator: Re: Elevator
item.content:encoded:
Heyo! I'll come and crit your draft you. Keep in mind I'm not clincal tone pro, so this'll largely be a 'what I think in general' type crit.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

SCP-XXXX is located at what was previously known as █████ Inc.

Generally, redacting/blackboxing something in the ConProcs (Special Containment Procedures) isn't a good idea. Realistically speaking, redacting information in the ConProcs doesn't make sense in-universe. These are the procedures—made as simple and basic as possible for personnel—for containing something. Redacting part of the information would just make the job more difficult than it needs to be.

Also, even out of ConProcs, I don't really see a reason to redact the name of a location. In universe, you're being granted clearance to read a classified article. Knowing where it came from usually isn't going to be that bad.

and administered Class A Amnestic.

Put 'a' between 'administered' and 'class'.

Following the unauthorized use of SCP-XXXX, no personnel under level four clearance are allowed in the same building as SCP-XXXX.

Probably a personal thing, but 'below level four clearance' sounds better than 'under'.

elevator shaft.The

Put a space between 'shaft.' and 'The'.

The elevator itself is comprised of steel and has seven buttons on the inside of it.

Remove 'itself'. Intuition says it's a tad unclinical to put it there.

SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator but when button seven is pressed the person(s) inside the elevator will be taken to the place they most desire to go.

'most desire to go' sounds off.
Let's try, 'SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator, but when the seventh button is pressed, the person(s) inside will be transported to a location they subconsciously desire.'

Inside is a GPS that records the places it has gone.

Let's try, 'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously traversed locations.'

The elevator will not work without it.

'The elevator will not function without the GPS.'
That said, I'm not sure how to feel about this line. I assume the GPS is just planted in the elevator. Also, this implies that the personnel have tried…removing it? I don't see why they'd do that.

Places recorded have been The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.

I think you can merge this with an earlier sentence to turn it into:
'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously explored locations, examples including The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.'

It's cleaner and smoother.

In all instances the elevator returns within 20 minutes after leaving the facility area.

Puts a comma after 'instances'

Always talked of "the fields".

Hmmm you can change 'of' to 'about' and it would be better, but it still sounds unclinical.

Maybe, 'Frequently mentioned a location he referred to as, 'the fields.'

personnel.Camera feed was choppy but the surroundings were normal.

Space after 'personnel.'

You should bold out 'Dr. Spencer's Diary' whenever you write down the entries. It makes it stand out and look cleaner.

'Foundation' should be capitalized because it's a proper noun.

The elevators GPS showed the word unkown on the location.

'GPS displayed 'unknown' as the location.'

Results: D-7586 appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.

I don't really like the way this is worded. 'Appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.'

You could just say that D-7586 died from exposure to outer space. It's been stated plainly thus far that the elevator takes you to where you want to go.

'Presume: suppose that something is the case on the basis of probability.'

There really isn't much probability here.

Apologies if this part sounds kinda overly nitpicky.

D-4576 was a surfer. She lived on the beach and says that is where her heart is. D-4576 is very kind to all personnel considering the situation she is in.

Clinical tone is meant to portray something as emotionlessly as possible. This passage reads a little too much like normal prose.
We could change it to, 'D-4576 once had a significant interest in surfing. She lived on a beach prior to becoming D-Class. She has been cooperative thus far.'

Even then, I'm not sure mentioning the cooperative part is necessary. Unless she shown shown be to uncooperative beforehand.

When D-4576 arrived back at the facility she was covered in sand. She stated it was the best day she has had in forever. Her dopamine levels were extremely high.

Second sentence is too emotional. Adjectives like 'extremely' are usually non-clinical.

Test 4 reads…super awkwardly. As well as the diary entry beforehand.

Also, the reference to SCP-682 wasn't a good move because references/cross-links nowadays are frowned upon.

This was a strange piece to critique, considering this is a greenlit idea with a draft from over a year ago. I looked at the edit history and see that it was updated a few days ago, yes, but it still feels…strange. I'll detail this more in my final thoughts collapsible.

+Final Thoughts
-Final Thoughts

All in all, I'm not sure how to feel about this. 'Get in thing and go to desired/weird locale at push of button/drop of hat' isn't anything new, but it's always the execution that matters more than the concept. Everything has already been done in storytelling history, it's about what you do with a thing to differentiate it that makes it special.

But from what I've seen of your current draft, it's really standard with sub-clinical tone, bizarre and not really believable diary entries and a plot that essentially equates to 'these test logs freak me out and I'm afraid I might die. GG, fuck this.'

I should let you know that I, myself, am still pretty new here and I wasn't here in 2019; I joined a few months ago as of me writing this down. From what I've heard and seen, generic testing logs with little information aren't really good anymore.

I've heard one person say that testing logs aren't really good anymore, period, but like I think you could make this SCP work if you…say…

Did more in depth logs with video logs and such. Strap a video cam to some D-Class, have them go through some stuff and extend each test log to being a mini-adventure. Pretty standard stuff, but there's always an audience for that.

Also, you'll need to incorporate the researcher more organically into the story rather than have them write some extremely barebones diary entries.

Maybe they could maintain communication with the test D-Class subjects during test logs?

From what I've seen of your current logs, they essentially stick D-class in the thing, wave goodbye and tell them to be back before dinner. That doesn't really make sense considering the D-Class can just leave and not come back.

All in all, I hope everything I wrote made sense and I hope I helped. Good luck with this piece. I hope you continue pursuing this because it's nice to contribute to a lovely site like this ^_^

item.title: Any improvements?: Any improvements?
item.content:encoded:

Item #: SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Keter Class

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is to be kept in a 50ft x 50ft Titanium room designed to look like a grazing field. The room is big enough to suit SCP-XXXX running needs. Steel shackles are to be locked to SCP-XXXX hind legs to at least slow it down. Reinforced sliding steel doors are locked in place when SCP-XXXX goes on its rampage. Two foundation agents who have taken courses on exorcism and have been dispatched by their teacher are to be kept at SCP-XXXX's containment cell at all times.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a male horse who has the ability to open a pocket dimension inside its underbelly. SCP-XXXX is normally friendly and isn't easily agitated. due to the side affects of the pocket dimension, It will go on a rampage once a week. This rampage usually lasts 1-2 hours. During the rampage, The pocket dimension opens and disembodied arms and hands burst from SCP-XXXX. Before recovery, these arms pillaged villages in Greece while SCP-XXXX is on its rampage. The foundation members managing SCP-XXXX's containment cell have given it the nickname, Trojan horse.

SCP-XXXX was discovered in [REDACTED], Greece on a farm where it was in is docile state. There had be a number of reports that week of a number of raids and pillages at neighboring villages. Later that week while field agents where following SCP-XXXX, They encountered it having its rampage. The pillage resulted in 10 civilians casualties and 2 agent casualties. The first recorded rampage the foundation had of SCP-XXXX lasted 1 hour. SCP-XXXX was recovered /9/10/2016/. Amnestics were given to all the involved villages.

[[collapsible show="+ FIRST BREACH. CLEARANCE LEVEL 5 NEEDED="- Title for hiding text"]]
[The first breach recorded resulted in [REDACTED] casualties. After the rampage, The foundation decided to teach a exorcism course to agents assigned to SCP-XXXX's containment cell. If SCP-XXXX should ever break containment, exorcism should be used to close the pocket dimension and have SCP-XXXX return to its docile state.]

D-Class Male

Sturdy rope was fasted to a harness which was worn by Samuel. The other end of the rope was tightened in a spool. a camera was the attached to his head. Samuel proceeded to travel into the pocket dimension that was forced open by the Field agents. When Samuel reached the other side, The camera was illuminated by a green hue. thousands of corpses could be seen in the distance. Samuel was given the other to go forward, which he heeded. The experiment was cut short because The D-class subject fell into a vat of acid under the platform he arrived at. When the footage is slowed down, A Stone throne could be seen behind the corpses. The foundation experts believe the pocket dimension to Be the Greek version of the underworld. ]

item.title: ELEPHANT HIDE: Re: ELEPHANT HIDE
item.content:encoded:
Sorry, I forgot to check this post for a while.

I think you definitely had a point saying that the poems seemed too simple for cryptographers. I might remove the entire last addendum that mentions the cryptographers, to make it seem like the Foundation either hasn't noticed it or more likely, didn't think it was noteworthy.

The overall narrative I'm trying to convey is… well it's not really extensive to be completely honest. Essentially, there are "SOULS INSIDE THE SKIN", as referenced by the -1-3 instance. These "souls" are meant to portray the consciousness of a sort that would be displayed by those who were killed by the SCP. Eventually, they become self-aware and realize what purpose they are being put to. I realize this is a huge stretch for one reader to make by themselves, so I was planning on either allowing the reader to make their own assumptions about the -1 instances or simply explaining the -1 instances in the Discuss tab.

In my experience, more questions are what makes a thing unnerving and unpredictable, however, I take it that there are simply too many questions based on your response. I agree with all of your line by line crit, and I really want to thank you for giving this SCP a critical eye!

item.title: Air Reconditioning Unit: Re: Air Reconditioning Unit
item.content:encoded:
Hello, gamer! Let's address a few of your points here.

[+] Reply time!
[-] Reply time!

didn't want to buck the trend

Not saying trends are always a bad thing (hell, the SCP article format is a trend in and of itself), but when the trend is almost always something that is not ideal, you probably want to stay away from that.

Also helped for calculating some math in regards to the amount of time it takes for this skip to alter the air in a room or add anomalous gas to the atmosphere, since 5 is a prime number and all.

…There was math involved? In all seriousness, I don't see anything in your description that contributes to the math involved here. There was no mention of how fast the fan converts things (not in terms of time, but in terms of how fast the air flows). Yes, the test logs give us a timeframe of how long it takes for the fan to finish converting air, but it gives us an expression we can solve, not an equation we can check. From what I can gather (and definitely correct me if I'm wrong), you were using the room measurements and the airflow to determine the amount of time it would take for it to convert air. However, the airflow is never mentioned, so the math you did literally doesn't matter because there's nothing to be wrong about (you know, cause it's not "solved" in the article yet). If you've forgotten to include the airflow, be sure to include it in your description so that your Special Containment Procedures make sense. Thanks for clearing up your reasons for including the measurements though, I get it now (though I'm still a little bit apprehensive considering that these are Special Containment Procedures and are not meant for testing, but you do you lol).

I have seen articles have revised containment procedures listed at the bottom sometimes accompanied by the words 'pending approval' and that was the thing I was aiming for with that.

Sort of the same thing as the trend idea I mentioned above, except it's not a bad thing. There's a reason those "Pending Approval" procedures are at the bottom. They're not in action yet. Special Containment Procedures are there for something that you should do in case of an emergency. However, the "Pending Approval" procedures are just that. Pending approval. It's good to keep them in mind, but they aren't strictly necessary. I don't see (or rather, it's not clarified) why your revised containment procedures aren't strictly necessary at the time of the article. If it's pending approval, clarify that.

Also I was worried that the revision may give something away in regards to the story, for now they stay where they are but I'm 50/50 about moving them.

Let's talk about the foreshadowing aspect of Special Containment Procedures. Generally, good containment procedures should give you a general idea of what the anomaly is like. You have a fire anomaly? Use fire-resistant materials. It gives you an idea of what the anomaly is without spoiling it. I'm not great at foreshadowing myself, but doing it right shouldn't give away your story too badly.

Your critique here was super helpful with that, and the lines you have pointed out as superfluous or lacklustre have been altered with your feedback. I'm hoping it's an improvement over the original!

No problem! And yes, I've just looked over it, and it's made improvements over the original. The one I can most easily point out the improvements on (that isn't to say nothing else improved, this is just the one I can most easily explain) is the one about some of the oxygen in the atmosphere being non-breathable. That part worked really well considering how the SCP was discovered. This is what you should continue doing, giving the reader pieces of the puzzle and having them connect them.

Overall though, nice revision! Keep getting feedback and you'll have a successful article in no time.

item.title: SCP-148 “Shini” concept draft: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies, authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for feedback on a full draft.

Please first go to the Ideas forum and read the required forum guidelines, or go to the chat and give a quick summary of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you ensure that the premise is something that will be successful with the community audience.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Air Reconditioning Unit: Re: Air Reconditioning Unit
item.content:encoded:
Hi there, thanks for the reply and critique! Let me start off with clearing up a couple of minor points. First, I did originally try to draft this using the typical SCP-XXXX placeholder but it was ruining my focus on the draft as I couldn't make it flow properly with those X's bothering me, so I went with a provisional number instead. Its purely a measure to ease my writing conscience. And a lot of the SCPs here seem to use 5x5x5 in their containment design anyway, didn't want to buck the trend. Also helped for calculating some math in regards to the amount of time it takes for this skip to alter the air in a room or add anomalous gas to the atmosphere, since 5 is a prime number and all.

As for the revised containment protocols, yeah you're probably right that they should be at the top but I was hesitant, I have seen articles have revised containment procedures listed at the bottom sometimes accompanied by the words 'pending approval' and that was the thing I was aiming for with that. Also I was worried that the revision may give something away in regards to the story, for now they stay where they are but I'm 50/50 about moving them.

Now for the meat amongst the potatoes! You hit one of my biggest concerns/weaknesses on the head, I do struggle with show vs. tell a lot. It's not an easy thing for me to overcome and its not from lack of trying. Your critique here was super helpful with that, and the lines you have pointed out as superfluous or lacklustre have been altered with your feedback. I'm hoping it's an improvement over the original!

item.title: SCP-148 “Shini” concept draft: O
Gears Centric Tale: Re: Gears Centric Tale
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

This feels longer than it needs to be and shorter than it needs to be simultaneously: if I had to describe it, I would say that the focus is wrong throughout; or perhaps that it lacks focus. It feels like this is meant as a retrospective of the whole of gears life, covering his entire growth as a person and how he went from being meek and timid at the start to a cold machine at the end, except all the bits that actually convey that change and growth have been cut.

Like, we have the introduction of his relationship with his wife here but not the end; so there's no impetus for him to shut off emotions because of that; which means his actual growth from warm and caring to cold is offscreen. Even before this, you have things that feel like they should be big impetuses for change, like the Cheyenne Point visit, that feel like they don't really do much.

Even then, the focus isn't quite directly on this so it just feels…iffy? It feels like this needs some kinda opening establishing why this story is being told; like, it's kinda cliche but perhaps intermingling the present time stuff with like. an interview at the end of the arc kinda, probing into why Gears is like this now say; so the progression is like. stylised versions of his retelling or w/e.

At the end of the day, I guess my biggest question is really just 'what do you expect a reader to get out of this?'

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

A single car wove through the vast green forest, its green exterior blending in with the earthly surroundings.

something about 'its green exterior' feels off to me and I can't quite put my finger on what; I think it might be the relatively formal sounding 'exterior' or possibly the repetition of 'green' but??

It crunched over rocks, making too much noise for it be so close to a Foundation site. But no one really cared, as no one really lived out here anyway.

The introduction of someone who might care (the foundation site) and then immediate dismissal of there being someone who might hear it feels…iffy?

It rumbled, it's tires too smooth and its brakes too slow but you didn't care too much.

this is a really jarring sentence; the way it flows from like, the passive description of stuff happening to the sudden second person is wild, particularly since it's not clear from here where 'you' is in this story yet.

barely revealing Site-19 with Research Wing 3A being constructed.

something about the 'with Research Wing 3A being constructed' here feels very iffy; I think it's that it kinda implies "Site-19 contains Research Wing 3A and both are being constructed", as opposed to "Site-19 is ahead, with a new research wing being constructed"; but I think also it's just a iffy time thing where there's kinda this big broad process at the end following a narrow arrival thing?

Maybe 'where Research Wing 3A is being constructed.' would work better?

It made you feel genuine, as though he really was a top-level researcher attempting to save the world

pronoun switch mid sentence from 'you' to 'he'

instead of an ambitious junior-researcher who

the sound of your voice, and the smell of alcohol. Was that a Jack Daniels?

'a Jack Daniels' here implies you mean like 'a bottle of jack', whereas if you cut the 'a' it implies 'the smell of jack', which is what you want, I think

They all had different assignments, but the way Site-19 was laid out, there was one long main corridor before it split off.

This feels like it's a tad overconcise; with it needing just a few more words to set out what is happening; or perhaps:

They all had different assignments, but because of the way Site-19 was laid out, they had to walk together down the main corridor before they each went their separate ways

The problem with this is also pronouns: 'they' doesn't include 'you', and you'll want to use 'You all' here instead, assuming you keep up the second person thing.

Kondraki was assigned to Dr. Cann, who headed research for 408. But it was widely known that he let his assistants take control of all of the work

this implies that Kondraki is one of the assistants, not the person with assistants

You were assigned to Agent Fritz Willie, and was told he was needed to contain SCP-106.

the 'was told he was needed' feels really oddly phrased, like, on the one hand, it feels like it's meant to be 'you' but on the other, something like "You were assigned to Agent Fritz Willie to help with the containment of SCP-106" would read better.

while you was doing paperwork asking for a new desk

'while you were filling in paperwork to get a new desk' would read better here; 'was' should be 'were' at least though this generally uses present tense throughout so 'are' would be the best.

He vaguely smelled of vodka.

I'd generally not split the verb/subject like this (i.e., use 'smelled vaguely' over 'vaguely smelled')

I'm turning 34, today, Charlie. I've been working here for.. fourteen years. Fresh outta the Marines.

20 feels young to leave the marines; it's only a couple of years of service depending on when he signed up.

"Don't be a fucking pussy, now."

The now feels weird here; like, it's not quite a command to have a drink now but it's also not quite flowing from the previous thing; and I'd probably cut it

"Commencing interview. Interviewer, Rachel Adams.

I'd probably name the interviewer before now; this introduction kinda makes it feel like how she looks is more important than who she is and it feels iffy

I said, no. There were no fucking flaws in my plan. The stupid fucking D-Class decided to insert the needle into the skip when the Anchors were running low on power, and then that woke up the bastard and-

There's no indication of how much time passed between the last chapter and now but this feels like a huge character shift: where Gears was kinda, timid and new in the previous section, he's now rude and aggressive; and it doesn't help that we're given like…no leading context to establish how he feels before this

with the bureaucratic nonsense that just impedes people and blames doctors for things they didn't see coming

this is the kinda statement that feels jarring compared to the opening; where we see two different people drinking on the job and a general laissez-faire feeling.

I will not listen to you whine because you decided to fuck up on a containment procedures plan.

'decided' feels weird here; like Gears chose to do a bad job deliberately over like, making a mistake or w/e. It also feels weird here cos the implication of the first section is that Gears had overdone the containment?

May I remind you I am here from the Ethics Committee

This feels altogether too late into this interview for this to be brought up now

and proposing termination.

It feels…kinda inappropriate for someone to be like "I am going to propose we kill you" to someone else?

Something you still thought about decades later, when tears didn't touch your face or you managed to smile. You were sent to Cheyenne Point Psychiatric Center

mentioning 'decades' and then following it up with a place gives the impression that he is going to spend decades there, not like, two years.

and returned to bed.

You slowly walked down

this feels weird cos the first bit implies he has done it already; whereas you then follow it up with a description of him getting into bed.

You have been sent back to active research duty and is immediately assigned a project to 914.

'and are immediately assigned to a project on SCP-914' would be clearer and more grammatically correct.

You note that all the experiments are just sticking things found inside researcher's pockets into the machine.

You've been briefed that you are now the new project head, which is something asof a surprise considering this is your first day back and you contained a monumental containment breach two years ago.

Should the 'contained' not be 'caused'?

Something about the previous two paragraphs made me feel like a length of time had passed, I think the "It feels.. good, to make a difference." implied to me that Gears had spent a bunch of time working on this already and so it actually being just after he returns feels odd

You felt anger and disbelief. This is how his dad repaid him.

another switch to 'he'

making you head on a research project instead of picking up the phone and saying Hello.

'of a research project' feels better to me but your call.

Charles Ogden Gears was

um i think you've forgotten to finish writing this psych report? It kinda feels weirdly jammed in here at the moment too but??

It's been five months since you had gotten married, and you've loved every single day.

This feels like a weirdly jarring way to introduce Gears' wife, like…it skips past 'first meeting' and 'falling in love' and straight to 'married' and it feels…too much of a jump maybe?

This whole section here feels weirdly positioned; it's very idyllic and there's no real … build up to it or anything
